Bench: Surya Kant, J.K. Maheshwari

 In The Supreme Court Of India
 Civil Appellate Jurisdiction
 Civil Appeal No.2672/2011
 Bihari Lal 
 Versus
 Land Acquisition Collector 
 O R D E R

1. The land owned by the appellant within the Revenue Estate of Village Sohana, District S.A.S.
Nagar (Mohali), Punjab was a part of the land measuring 934.81 acres which was proposed to be acquired by the State of Punjab vide Notification dated 21022020 issued under Section 4 of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894 (in short, `the Act).
The aforesaid land was eventually acquired vide Award dated 17052001.

The appellant and other landowners, being dissatisfied with the compensation, filed References under Section 18 of the Act and the Reference Court granted the compensation at the rate of Rs.17,00,000/ per acre.
The appellant and other affected landowners were still dissatisfied, hence they filed First Appeals before the High Court.
Vide impugned Judgment dated 02032009, the High Court marginally increased the compensation to Rs.19,85,700/ per acre.
2. The appellant as well as some of his coowners were still Date: 2023.02.13 16:52:06 IST

aggrieved of not getting just and fair compensation, hence approached this Court.

3. Some of the appeals came up for hearing before a Coordinate Bench on 15012014 titled Paramjit Panag And Others vs. State of Punjab (2015) 17 SCC 342 and the same were allowed in the following terms: Para 5.

Accordingly, we enhance the compensation payable to the landowner to another Rs.2,00,000/ per acre payable by the Greater Mohali Area Development Authority (for Short GMADA) with interest and solatium as prescribed under the statute from the date of the order passed by the High Court.
The said enhanced amount shall be deposited by GMADA within three months time from today.

opennyai_summary.facts:
1. The land owned by the appellant within the Revenue Estate of Village Sohana, District S.A.S.
Nagar (Mohali), Punjab was a part of the land measuring 934.81 acres which was proposed to be acquired by the State of Punjab vide Notification dated 21022020 issued under Section 4 of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894 (in short, `the Act).
The appellant and other landowners, being dissatisfied with the compensation, filed References under Section 18 of the Act and the Reference Court granted the compensation at the rate of Rs.17,00,000/ per acre.
The appellant and other affected landowners were still dissatisfied, hence they filed First Appeals before the High Court.
opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
In the peculiar facts and circumstances of the case, we are of the view that the compensation awarded by the High Court requires to be increased.
Following the dictum in Paramjit Panag And Others vs. State of Punjab, this Court granted the same amount of enhanced compensation in Civil Appeal Nos.67446758/2022 titled Harpal Singh & Others vs. State of Punjab & Others decided on 23092022.
5.
opennyai_summary.decision:
Accordingly, we enhance the compensation payable to the landowner to another Rs.2,00,000/ per acre payable by the Greater Mohali Area Development Authority (for Short GMADA) with interest and solatium as prescribed under the statute from the date of the order passed by the High Court.
The said enhanced amount shall be deposited by GMADA within three months time from today.
After hearing learned counsel for the parties and on perusal of the material placed on record, we find that the instant Civil Appeal deserves to be allowed in part, being squarely covered by the decisions of this Court in Paramjit Panag (supra) and Harpal Singh (supra) cases.
6. Ordered accordingly.
7.
The appellant is held entitled to further enhancement of compensation of Rs.2,00,000/ per acre for his acquired land over and above the rate granted by the High Court.
8. The respondents including the Greater Mohali Area Development Authority will pay the enhanced amount of compensation along with interest and solatium as per prescribed rate under the 1894, Act from the date of order passed by the High Court.
The enhanced amount shall be deposited with the Reference Court within three months from the date of receipt of a copy of this Order and shall be disbursed to the appellant without any delay.
